correctness.rationale: Every fixed barycentric vector has support a union of translation cosets. If a subgroup contains a vector of weight >=3 no orbit is a simplex; otherwise subgroup rank <=2 by a full binary support argument. Rank-one coset compatibility is explicitly linearly isomorphic to Q_(n-1) for generators of weights one and two. Rank-two admissible codes (coordinate 2-plane and 3-coordinate even plane) have pairwise incompatible distinct cosets. Independent exhaustive orbit reconstruction passed 125 admissible groups through n=6; the universal proof, not the test, covers all n>=3.

value.rationale: This is the entire subgroup-indexed geometric fixed-space profile for a natural infinite equivariant topological family, not a finite arbitrary slice. In positive rank one it detects exponentially many fixed-space circles despite the ambient space being a wedge of 3-spheres; at rank two it determines exact disconnectedness for simultaneous stabilizers. Neither phenomenon is determined by ordinary Betti numbers or the full rational ordinary homology representation alone.
